reported_intentional_changes.heading: Changes and intentional differences
reported_intentional_changes.text:
- List responses retain upstream metadata and continuation fields in addition to
  the existing items/count output. Unknown item fields remain lossless. Typed
  projection validates the actual fields used for display and target selection;
  malformed list/item shapes return `api/invalid_response` instead of silently
  becoming an empty list or targeting a malformed item.
- Name resolution requires an exact unique match with a command ID and rejects
  a response marked `has_more:true`. No arbitrary first match is mutated. The
  endpoint is documented as unpaginated, with a maximum of 100 commands; if that
  backend contract changes, pagination support must be verified before by-name
  writes can use incomplete results. Reads retain the continuation for inspection.
- By-name updates compare the entire supplied replacement objects with the live
  state already fetched for resolution and return `action:unchanged` without
  PATCH when equal. The force collision path does the same after its existing
  POST/list steps. Description replacement includes the entire i18n map; an
  omitted existing language or an unknown existing replacement field prevents a
  false no-op. Omitted top-level fields never imply deletion.
- Direct-ID updates keep their original write-only permission contract and issue
  PATCH without an additional read. No local lock or comparison claims remote
  concurrency protection. The read/compare/write sequence has no backend ETag or
  conditional-write guarantee.
- Receipt classification is intentionally conservative: a code 40000000 collision
  remains unknown in the shared journal. A force collision followed by PATCH or
  no-op therefore exits 22 and preserves the full `updated`/`unchanged` result
  with `ok:false`; the later step never erases earlier evidence. Unknown responses
  are not retried. This limitation needs domain receipt interpretation before a
  collision rerun can report fully reconciled success; no parallel journal was added.
- Artifacts use the shared versioned result container and current identity/app
  binding. Full localized content and continuation survive projection. Existing
  destinations and known credential-bearing fields are rejected; mutation commands
  reject `--save-result` before dispatch. There is no Application artifact import
  command, and result containers are not accepted as replacement payloads.

- Domain-known POST previews and plugin metadata/download reads are explicitly excluded from mutation journaling. Actual schema/sync/content writes retain conservative receipts. Partial/malformed SQL outcomes use the shared SQL receipt classifier and pass the process regression.

reported_intentional_changes.heading: Intentional interface differences and safety evidence
reported_intentional_changes.text:
- `--skip-unchanged` on record updates adds an explicit optional `base:record:read` prerequisite; legacy write scopes are unchanged. It compares exact submitted cells in a validated backend matrix and sends zero mutations when unchanged. Missing/ambiguous/incomplete reads stop the whole update before writing; omitted fields never delete data. Numbers are compared conservatively by token, so `1` and `1.0` may still write. Read and write are not atomic; other clients may race.
- All Base JSON object/array inputs now use number-preserving decoding. Syntax errors retain their original typed cause. Role response inner/double-encoded JSON likewise retains numeric precision.
- NDJSON no longer changes null selections/users to `[]`, null checkboxes to false, or local datetime strings to RFC3339. Manifest physical types describe nullable arrays/booleans; null and empty counts are separate. Numeric bounds preserve exact source values, approximate averages are marked; unparsed datetime statistics are explicit. Name collisions (including a user field named `record_id`) and duplicate field IDs fail instead of dropping values. Raw JSON reads still preserve those native matrices.
- List/search NDJSON requires explicit `has_more`; missing continuation evidence fails instead of treating the result as complete. Batch-get remains explicitly selected-record scoped. The 2,000 requested-row NDJSON ceiling remains; continuation metadata is retained and larger workflows page explicitly.
- `+record-import` consumes the existing shared result artifact containing `sheets-data/v1`, verifies current observed identity/tenant binding, checks exact complete source extent and destination field identity/type, and appends in 200-row batches. Every column is explicitly mapped. Unformatted primitive text/number/checkbox cells are supported; typed import rejects decimals that cannot round-trip through the documented Base double storage (including 9007199254740993); formulas, formatting (including date styles), rich/identity/object cells or unsupported conversion types are rejected before any write. Null, empty and omitted values remain distinct; a destination default that would fill an omitted source cell is rejected. It creates records every invocation, with no implicit business-key matching or deletion.
- Optional import `--output` saves all observed record IDs via existing invocation-scoped exclusive FileIO, keeping the 10,000-row payload outside stdout. Destination collision is checked before writes and races cannot overwrite files. If final report save fails, full observed effects remain on stdout with a typed failure. Unknown batches stop; IDs must be unique across the entire import, and an ID repeated from an earlier batch leaves the later batch unresolved without dispatching the next batch. Receipts are evidence, never automatic replay inputs.

reported_intentional_changes.text:
Existing nearby units cover Markdown/rich images and workspace boundaries, automatic self attendee inclusion and rollback, attendee user/chat/resource/third-party projections, RSVP, ownership transfer, room availability/approval handling, search and attendee pagination, all-day dates, explicit offsets/timezone warnings, free/busy merging and suggestions, recurring master/instance/exception classification, exception pagination/deduplication/caps, UNTIL/COUNT handling and exception ordering/cancellation. No personal-state legacy live tests were executed.

Target and recurring-scope validation now precede local description image resolution, preventing image uploads for an ambiguous update. A nearby regression checks that the scope error wins before an absent local image could be read.

The new change suppresses a single-event exact replacement when the already fetched event has the same nonempty summary/rich description/recurrence and requested timed timestamps. The response adds `no_op:true`; no event PATCH or attendee notification is sent. Explicit `--notify=true`, explicit clears and attendee add/remove requests retain their effects. A synthetic instance reconstructed from its master is marked internally and cannot establish no-op evidence. This does not claim atomic compare-and-swap or protection from concurrent external edits.

Whole-series updates retain their existing semantics: each exception may have an independent override, and an equal master value is not evidence that every exception matches. This-and-following is an explicit split with deletion/truncation/new-series effects. Whole-series per-exception exact no-op suppression is not implemented; the current exception projection has only IDs and start times. No blanket no-op claim is made for these workflows. Explicit clear still sends the clear even when a fetched value is empty.

The full process suite uses the real authsidecar production CLI, private local config/work state, and an HTTP fixture that never forwards to Feishu. It covers every shortcut, every frozen generic method, successful event lifecycle/readback/cleanup, rich Unicode and precision-preserving attachments, full result artifact identity/tenant binding, all four free/busy views, constrained room/suggestion reads, pagination continuations, three recurring update/delete strategies, inherited following-series attachment/check-in/third-party attendee preservation, ambiguity before writes, scope denial, partial multi-step effects and malformed-response unknown outcomes without replay. Generic method fixtures assert requests and full response preservation; they are not claims about actual backend side effects.

`attendees/batch_delete` remains conservatively unknown (exit 22) even for a successful envelope; the fixture explicitly asserts that result. Without endpoint-specific item evidence the CLI cannot prove all removals. Other synchronous success receipts acknowledge requests, not downstream notification delivery or complete workflow guarantees. Calendar creation retains the reference compensating deletion on attendee failure; it is not an atomic transaction. Crash/cancellation mechanics are shared foundation contracts; Calendar worker cancellation has nearby unit coverage, but abrupt process interruption during Calendar recurrence is not independently injected by this suite.

reported_intentional_changes.heading: Changes and semantics
reported_intentional_changes.text:
Existing complete domain implementations are reused. Draft replacements now
compare the original and patched MIME using the same serializer before PUT.
Identical supported replacement results return `no_op:true` and do not write.
Unchanged plain/HTML bodies keep their original MIME entity instead of marking
it dirty, and a matching decoded Unicode subject retains its encoded header. This comparison avoids treating base64 padding or line endings in
the backend transport representation as user changes. It is deliberately
conservative: append, uploads, attachment removals, signatures and calendar
operations keep their explicit effects. Changed content still uses the existing
MIME-safe pipeline and preserves untouched attachments and custom headers.

Template updates similarly skip PUT when their complete typed representation
is unchanged and no attachments were uploaded. Rule replacement/state no-op is
reused from the reference. None of these checks provides optimistic locking;
concurrent writers can overwrite each other after the read.

Mail reads inherit compact lossless JSON, projection and full result artifacts.
A 21-ID process fixture verifies two bounded batch reads, stable order, a missing
ID, rich HTML retained in the artifact and no receipt on the POST read. Triage
exposes its returned count, mailbox and continuation rather than claiming a
complete mailbox snapshot. Generic artifacts are not draft/template patch files.

Send operations are never deduplicated from equal content. Process fault
injection checks one dispatch for accepted, scope-rejected, malformed and lost
responses, plus partial send and account-level abort. Shared receipts describe
API acknowledgement, not downstream delivery. Asynchronous/batch uncertainty
retains the foundation's conservative classification and never authorizes replay.

reported_intentional_changes.heading: Intentional new interface and data integrity
reported_intentional_changes.text:
`+data-export --spreadsheet-token TOKEN --sheet-id ID --range A1:D100 --save-result PATH` adds a native, versioned, fully bounded cell artifact. `+data-import` consumes that artifact with explicit target identity and extent. The artifact contains `feishu-cli-next/sheets-data/v1` inside the shared bound result envelope. Import requires verified current tenant/identity binding. It rejects incomplete or incompatible artifacts, validates every conversion before any write, and emits `noop`, changed-cell and acknowledged-page evidence. Read pages contain at most 5,000 cells; the supported explicit extent is at most 1,000,000 cells and 5,000 columns. This is not a snapshot or compare-and-swap guarantee.

Native JSON preserves decimal tokens, large integer values, leading zeros in strings, booleans, formula fields, styles and field presence. Omitted cell fields are patches, not inferred deletion. reported_intentional_changes.heading: Corrections and effect boundaries
reported_intentional_changes.text:
Raw authoring now decodes numbers with `UseNumber`, fixing float64 corruption of
values such as `9007199254740993` and `1.234567890123456789`. Both supported raw
input envelopes retain all nested values. The decoder still rejects trailing JSON
or garbage with a typed `--source` validation failure. Update dry-run now includes
its supplied `client_token`, matching execution for every format. The previously
unselected required-selector regression is named for the deterministic section
runner so it executes at the boundary.

These are fidelity and preview corrections, not interface replacements. Existing
native node/image/style/source payloads remain intact; no simplified node schema
or conversion is introduced. A generic `--save-result` container is not an import
payload and is rejected without dispatch. Exported raw `--output` JSON is the
existing explicit import representation; backend-generated identities after
creation remain subject to backend semantics.

An unchanged-content no-op is deliberately **not claimed**. The reference update
API creates nodes; overwrite explicitly replaces content. Source equality alone
does not prove the complete current board is identical, and the write-only scope
does not prove read access or current edit permission. A local equality shortcut
would bypass backend permission checks and could omit unrelated nodes. Append
always dispatches; explicit empty overwrite dispatches even when already empty.
Process tests observe 1→2→1→0→0 nodes through independent reads and five writes.
Expand no-op behavior only with an exact complete-state and permission-aware
backend contract; do not infer it from image/source equality. There is no
conditional revision flag or concurrency guarantee from receipt locks.

Receipts are supplied by the shared runtime before dispatch. Synthetic process
faults prove a permission rejection is confirmed-unapplied, malformed/lost
responses remain unknown without retry, and item failure evidence is not promoted
to complete success. An acknowledged API envelope is request evidence, not proof
of live rendering fidelity or preserved backend identity. Unknown overwrite is
never automatically replayed.
